leads.candidate: Zomereik (Pedunculate Oak, Quercus robur) in front of Kasteel Groeneveld
leads.why_not_shipped: Single-sourced this pass (monumentaltrees.com archived park page only, girth 4.70m @1.3m, height 27.40m). No second independent source or planting date found yet. A solid candidate for a next pass, would be a clean single-stem entry (vs. the ensemble/grove entries already shipped) if a second source and firmer coordinates turn up.

leads.candidate: Beech copse west of Kasteel Groeneveld (multiple large Fagus sylvatica, girths 4.00-5.05m, ids 19447/19449/19451/19450)
leads.why_not_shipped: Single-sourced (same archived park page); no ages, no second source, and unclear whether this copse reads as one collectible destination distinct from the already-shipped Copper Beech (brn_004) and Tulip Tree Grove (brn_003), or is really the same general west-of-castle woodland. Needs a closer look, possibly a site photo, before deciding whether it is its own entry or should be folded into brn_004.

leads.candidate: European Larch (Larix decidua) at Kasteel Groeneveld, id 3423, girth 2.88m, height 23m, two large nails embedded in the trunk
leads.why_not_shipped: Girth/height modest compared to the estate's other candidates; page itself notes it stands hemmed in by beeches and 'deserves to be freed'. Single-sourced, no age. A curiosity (the embedded nails) more than a clear remarkable-tree case; parked rather than pursued this pass.

leads.candidate: Cantonspark's remaining Pinetum specimens: Chestnut-leaved Oak (Quercus castaneifolia, id 3140, girth 4.15m/26.80m), Bald Cypress 'Fastigiatum' (Taxodium distichum, id 3115, girth 3.70m/23.00m), European White Elm (Ulmus laevis, id 3926, girth 3.65m/27.40m), a second Dawn Redwood (id 3927, girth 3.52m/22.90m), Veitch's Silver Fir (Abies veitchii, id 3925), Velvet Maple (Acer velutinum, id 3928), Sassafras (Sassafras albidum, id 14156)
leads.why_not_shipped: All single-sourced from one 2014 archived monumentaltrees.com index page (no individual pages archived, live site blocked by Cloudflare); no second source or age found this pass. Genuinely promising, an unusually rich pinetum, but ran out of budget this pass to verify each individually. Good target for a next Baarn pass, especially the White Elm (Ulmus laevis is increasingly rare due to Dutch elm disease, would be a strong story) and the Sassafras (unusual for the Netherlands).

leads.candidate: Paleis Soestdijk park's monumental tree route
leads.register_id: monumentaltrees 1096_paleissoestdijk (Soest slug, but palace address is Baarn per brief)
leads.why_not_shipped: Confirmed genuinely open to the public again: palace garden Friday-Sunday 11:00-19:00 (as of 24 July 2026), paid entry EUR 2.50, wheelchair accessible, with the estate's own guided walks specifically themed around its monumental trees. Not pursued to a verified entry this pass purely for time; this is very likely fruitful next time given the palace itself markets a tree route. Access should be stated honestly as paid, weekend-only, not daily/free like the other Baarn candidates.
